correctness.rationale: For every integer dimension \(d\ge3\) and every unordered two-distinct-edge deletion, an elementary d-edge-connectivity proof guarantees finite Kirchhoff index. Walsh spectral decomposition gives rational Green and squared-Green kernels at every Hamming distance. The heat-kernel integral makes successive differences positive and strictly decreasing, yielding exactly two automorphism classes per distance and identifying one candidate from each. Rank-two Woodbury gives a correctly normalized N-scaled rational increase, strictly monotone in both positive mixed-kernel entries. A likelihood-ratio tilt proves \(a_0>3a_1\) from \(d=3\) onward and \(b_0>3b_1\) from \(d=8\) onward, using the exact d=8 certificate \(1007/1204224\). The \(d=3,4,5,6,7\) rational differences are all strictly positive, directly reproducible. The packaged standalone checker replays rational base differences, independently compares grounded inverses for dimensions 3–5, and enumerates their entire unordered-edge-pair orbits. Finite testing is only corroborating; the universal step is proved analytically.

originality.rationale: The new claim is a strict, globally quantified two-edge interdiction classification for unit-conductance Boolean cubes. Full text of the most directly relevant hypercube resistance-index article was inspected, and the later complete-graph deletion paper was inspected in primary PDF text and page images. The former calculates the intact cube and certain graph transforms, while the latter treats a different base graph for which the edge-defect reduction does not imply the new cube orbit inequalities. The earlier hypercube leverage work uses shortest-path sums, not Kirchhoff index. Other published network-vulnerability claims address wheels, multipartite graphs, and bouquet failure motifs, not Boolean cube edge failures. Research-record and bibliographic searches found no exact or stronger match. Search nonreturns alone do not establish novelty; the mathematical differences and abstract-only risk are recorded.
residual_risks: Full text of Hamburger–Pippert–Weakley (1992) could not be inspected; its abstract explicitly treats a different distance metric but undisclosed related results are possible.
Specialized or unindexed articles, dissertations and independent mathematical proofs could establish equivalent or stronger hypercube two-link sensitivity results.
No independent expert originality check or audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The objective is total effective-resistance loss under two simultaneous physical link failures, a standard robustness/interdiction design question on hypercube interconnection topologies. Determining exactly which failure pair is worst among all dimension-dependent possibilities is not a prescribed numerical slice or ordinary normalization check. The theorem completely classifies all optimal attacks for infinitely many growing graphs, counts their multiplicity, and provides a closed finite-rational expression for damage. The nontrivial insight is strict dominance of incident failures over even parallel near-neighbor failures in every dimension despite competing Green-kernel terms in small dimensions.
